mainTopic: How each kind of holy property found in an עיר הנדחת is treated: altar animals, בכור and מעשר, תרומה, and מעשר שני
overview: The משנה said that holy property in an עיר הנדחת is redeemed. A ברייתא gives the details: altar animals die, בדק הבית items are redeemed, תרומה rots, and מעשר שני and holy writings are hidden away. רבי שמעון learns from 'its animals' and 'its spoils' that בכור, מעשר, and holy money are not the city's property at all. The גמרא asks why altar animals die instead of being sold after they get a מום. רבי יוחנן answers that a wicked person's offering is an abomination. ריש לקיש answers that these animals count as the owner's property, and the גמרא ends up applying this to קדשים קלים following רבי יוסי הגלילי. Next the גמרא explains which בכור and מעשר רבי שמעון means, and shows that שמואל disagrees. רב חסדא then explains which תרומה rots, and rewords his rule after רב יוסף objects. Finally, רב יוסף challenges רב חסדא's view that מעשר שני outside ירושלים belongs to Heaven. The גמרא answers that the משנה is about impure food bought with מעשר שני money inside ירושלים.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists what happens to each kind of holy property in the condemned city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about holy property in an עיר הנדחת, then brings a ברייתא that sorts the holy items into four groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the holy property in the city must be redeemed. The רבנן taught: if there were holy things in it, animals set aside for the altar must be left to die. Things set aside for the upkeep of the בית המקדש must be redeemed. תרומות must be left to rot. מעשר שני and holy writings must be put away (buried).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and brings a ברייתא that gives the details. Each type of holy item gets its own treatment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה just said 'redeem,' but the ברייתא shows that only בדק הבית items are redeemed. Altar animals cannot simply be redeemed, so they are left to die. Food and writings that cannot be burned along with the city are rotted or put away instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A city whose people mostly turned to idol worship; it is destroyed and its property burned (דברים פרק י״ג)
Animals set aside to be offered on the altar
The fund for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
They must be redeemed (bought out of their holiness with money)
They must be put away or buried in a respectful way

steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the משנה's word 'redeem' applies to everything. The ברייתא shows that only בדק הבית property is redeemed; altar animals are left to die.

phrases.english: And the consecrated property in it must be redeemed, etc.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ בָּהּ קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: If there were sacred offerings in it,
those consecrated for the altar must die;
those consecrated for Temple upkeep must be redeemed;
and terumot must be left to rot;
and second tithe and sacred writings must be put away.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ בָּהּ קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion of the משנה's line about holy property
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Altar animals die, בדק הבית items are redeemed, תרומות rot, and מעשר שני and holy writings are put away.

steps.title: רבי שמעון excludes firstborns, tithes and holy money from the city's property
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from the words 'its animals' and 'its spoils' that בכור, מעשר בהמה, and holy money are not counted as the city's property.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the פסוק says 'its animals.' That means not the animals of בכור and מעשר. It says 'its spoils.' That leaves out holy money and מעשר money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He uses words from the פסוקים to show that certain holy things are simply not part of the city's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'its' tells us the Torah only destroys what really belongs to the city. בכור, מעשר בהמה, and holy money belong to Heaven, not to the city's people. So they are left out of the destruction entirely.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its animals' (דברים 13:16)
'Its spoils' (דברים 13:17)
A firstborn kosher animal, which is holy from birth
'Except for' / 'to leave out'

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: “Its animals”
and not firstborn or tithe animals;
“its spoils”, except for consecrated money
and tithe money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A dissenting opinion within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Holy things that belong to Heaven (בכור, מעשר, holy money) are not the city's property and are not destroyed.

steps.title: Why kill the altar animals instead of selling them after they get a blemish?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ruling that altar animals must die and asks why. They could graze until they get a מום and then be sold, with the money going to communal gift offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: if there were holy animals for the altar in the city, they must die. But why should they die? Let them graze until they get a blemish, then sell them and use the money for gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats one line of the ברייתא so it can question it. It suggests a way to save the animals' value instead of wasting it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a holy animal that can't be offered is left to graze until it gets a מום. Then it is sold, and the money buys new offerings. The challenge is that this ordinary method should work here too, so letting them die seems like a needless loss.

keyTerms.meaning: They become blemished (and so unfit for the altar)
A voluntary gift offering, here bought with communal funds
'But why?'

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: הָיוּ בָּהּ קׇדְשֵׁי קֳדָשִׁים,
phrases.english: The Master said: If there were sacred offerings in it,
those consecrated for the altar must die.
But why must they die?
Let them graze until they become blemished,
and be sold, and their money go to gift offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the first ruling of the ברייתא to challenge it
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that altar animals in an עיר הנדחת must die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a standard way to save a holy animal's value (graze, blemish, sell, buy offerings), so killing it seems unnecessary.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a wicked person's offering is disgusting
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן answers that the animals must die because 'the offering of the wicked is an abomination.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: 'The offering of the wicked is an abomination.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers the question. These animals came from idol worshippers, so nothing about them may be used for the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals belonged to wicked people, so even their value is unwanted for offerings. The sale-and-gift method is closed off, and the animals are left to die.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The offering of the wicked is an abomination' (משלי 21:27)
Something disgusting or hateful

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
“The offering of the wicked is an abomination.”

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: זֶבַח רְשָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a פסוק showing the animals cannot be used for offerings at all
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The animals could be sold after a blemish and the money used for gift offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: Offerings of the wicked are rejected entirely, so they must die

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the animals still count as the owner's property
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש answers differently. The animals are still the owner's property, so they are destroyed with the rest of the city's property. He explains this as offerings the owner is responsible to replace, following רבי שמעון.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: it is the owner's property. Here we are dealing with offerings the owner must replace if lost, and this follows רבי שמעון, who says such offerings are the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a second answer. The animals die because they count as the city people's property, and that property is destroyed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a person promised 'I take upon myself an offering' (a נדר), he must replace the animal if something happens to it. Because of that responsibility, רבי שמעון treats the animal as still partly his. So it falls under 'the city's property,' which must be destroyed.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, רבי יוחנן's study partner and frequent disputant
'The owner's property.' The animal still counts as belonging to the person
He is responsible to replace them if they are lost or die

phrases.aramaic: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הוּא.
phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: It is the owner's property.
And here it is about offerings he is responsible to replace,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא דְּאָמַר: מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הוּא.
phrases.english: and it follows Rabbi Shimon, who says: It is the owner's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מָמוֹן בְּעָלִים הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the קשיא of step 3
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: offerings the owner must replace, which count as his property
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Altar animals are purely Heaven's and should be sold for gift offerings
steps.terutzMaskana: They are the owner's property and so are destroyed along with the city's property

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא is רבי שמעון, so the beginning cannot be
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks ריש לקיש's explanation. רבי שמעון appears at the end of the ברייתא as the one who disagrees, so the first part must be a different תנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the last part of the ברייתא is רבי שמעון, doesn't that mean the first part is not רבי שמעון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the claim that the first ruling follows רבי שמעון. It points to how the ברייתא is built.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון is named in the ברייתא as arguing against the opening ruling. So the opening ruling cannot be his own view. That knocks out the way step 5 explained ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a source
The opening part of a source

phrases.english: But since the latter part is Rabbi Shimon,
is the first part not Rabbi Shimon?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא מִדְּסֵיפָא רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן הִיא, רֵישָׁא לָאו רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the attribution to רבי שמעון in step 5
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the first ruling of the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון is named in the סיפא as disagreeing, so the רישא must be a different תנא.

steps.title: The ברייתא means קדשים קלים, following רבי יוסי הגלילי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains ריש לקיש a new way. The animals that die are קדשים קלים, and they count as the owner's property according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is talking about קדשים קלים, and it follows רבי יוסי הגלילי, who said: קדשים קלים are the owner's property.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps ריש לקיש's idea of 'the owner's property' but connects it to a different תנא and a different type of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי הגלילי holds that קדשים קלים (like שלמים) always belong to the owner. This is true even without any responsibility to replace them. So the ruling 'they must die' is about these lesser offerings, and it no longer needs רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of lesser holiness, such as שלמים
'According to the view of'

phrases.english: It is about offerings of lesser sanctity,
and according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
who said: Offerings of lesser sanctity are the owner's property.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּקָדָשִׁים קַלִּים, וְאַלִּיבָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by switching to a different תנא and case
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the ruling to a different תנא and narrows the case to קדשים קלים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling follows רבי שמעון about offerings one must replace
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling follows רבי יוסי הגלילי about קדשים קלים, which are the owner's property

steps.title: The most holy offerings are redeemed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws out the result of the new explanation. קדשי קדשים are not the owner's property, so they are not destroyed but redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what happens to the most holy offerings? They must be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the new explanation means for קדשי קדשים and answers: they are redeemed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only קדשים קלים count as the owner's property, so only they are destroyed with the city. קדשי קדשים belong to Heaven, so they are not part of the city's property, and they are redeemed instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Offerings of the highest holiness, such as עולה and חטאת
'What?'

steps.whatToRemember: According to ריש לקיש's final explanation, altar animals die only because they count as the city people's property. That is true of קדשים קלים according to רבי יוסי הגלילי. קדשי קדשים, which belong to Heaven, are redeemed. According to רבי יוחנן, they die because a wicked person's offering is rejected.

phrases.english: But offerings of the most sacred order, what about them?
They are redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of the explanation in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to ריש לקיש, קדשי קדשים in an עיר הנדחת are redeemed; only קדשים קלים, as the owner's property, die.

steps.title: Why not split the altar offerings themselves?
steps.stepSummary: If ריש לקיש is right that only קדשים קלים die and קדשי קדשים are redeemed, the ברייתא should have taught that split directly instead of contrasting with בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Instead of teaching at the end that בדק הבית items are redeemed, the ברייתא should have drawn a line within the altar offerings: קדשים קלים die, but קדשי קדשים are redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation of ריש לקיש from Step 7. It asks why the ברייתא did not teach its distinction in a simpler, closer way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Step 8, the ברייתא's ruling that 'animals die' covers only קדשים קלים, while קדשי קדשים are redeemed. If so, the ברייתא could have made that distinction inside the altar offerings themselves. Jumping all the way to בדק הבית seems unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather than teaching
The latter part of a teaching
Items set aside for upkeep of the בית המקדש, not for the altar
Let it make the distinction and teach it within the same category
In what case is this said? (a formula that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Rather than teaching in the latter clause:
items consecrated for Temple maintenance must be redeemed,
let it distinguish and teach within the same category itself:
phrases.notes: He means: draw the line inside the altar offerings themselves, without bringing in בדק הבית.

phrases.english: In what case are these words said?
With offerings of lesser sanctity,
but offerings of the most sacred order shall be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in light of the result in Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's explanation that only קדשים קלים die
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the real split is between קדשים קלים and קדשי קדשים, the ברייתא should have stated that split instead of contrasting with בדק הבית.

steps.title: The sin-offering whose owners died breaks the rule
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא could not say that all קדשי קדשים are redeemed, because a חטאת whose owners died is always left to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: Among קדשי קדשים there is the חטאת whose owners died, which is left to die. So the rule 'קדשי קדשים are redeemed' would not hold in every case.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Splitting the altar offerings would not give a clean rule, so the ברייתא used a distinction with no exceptions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the owners of a חטאת are killed with the city, that חטאת must die anyway under the general law of a חטאת whose owners died. So 'קדשי קדשים are redeemed' has an exception. The contrast with בדק הבית, by contrast, works in every case.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin-offering whose owners died, which is left to die
It goes to die
It is not a clear-cut rule for him (it has exceptions)

phrases.english: Since there is the sin-offering whose owners died,
which goes to die,
it is not clear-cut for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 9
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to an exception that blocks the suggested wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא could have split קדשים קלים from קדשי קדשים.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תנא prefers a distinction with no exceptions, and קדשי קדשים include the חטאת whose owners died, which dies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common principle: a תנא picks the wording that holds true in every case.

steps.title: Why does ריש לקיש reject רבי יוחנן's reason?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's reason is clear, since he has a פסוק. But why doesn't ריש לקיש use that same פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that רבי יוחנן does not explain like ריש לקיש, because of the פסוק 'the offering of the wicked is an abomination.' But why doesn't ריש לקיש explain like רבי יוחנן?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps back and compares the two explanations from Steps 4 and 5. It asks what ריש לקיש's reason is for not using רבי יוחנן's פסוק, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן has a clear source, so his choice needs no explaining. ריש לקיש chose a harder route through property rules and a specific תנא. The גמרא wants to know why he did not simply use the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (for this side)
'The offering of the wicked is an abomination' (משלי 21:27)
What is the reason?

phrases.english: Granted, Rabbi Yochanan
does not say like Reish Lakish,
since it is written: 'The offering of the wicked is an abomination.'
But Reish Lakish,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן?
phrases.english: what is the reason he does not say like Rabbi Yochanan?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא אָמַר כְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to compare the two answers given in Steps 4 and 5
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why ריש לקיש does not accept the reason of 'the offering of the wicked is an abomination'

steps.title: Once the animal is redeemed, it has changed
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש holds that the פסוק applies only to the original animal. Once it is redeemed and replaced, it is no longer the wicked person's offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: He could say: 'the offering of the wicked is an abomination' applies only when the offering is still in its original form. Here, once it is redeemed, it has changed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives ריש לקיש's reason. The פסוק cannot force the animals to die, because redeeming them would change them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal were redeemed, the money would buy a new offering. That new animal never belonged to the wicked person. So the פסוק does not apply, and ריש לקיש needs a different reason for why the animals die.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you
This applies only (in this case)
In their original, unchanged form
It has changed

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the animals die because of 'זבח רשעים תועבה.' ריש לקיש: that פסוק does not apply once the animal is redeemed, so they die only because they count as the owner's property.

phrases.english: He could say to you:
When we say 'the offering of the wicked is an abomination,'
that applies where they are in their original form,
but here,
since it has changed, it has changed.
phrases.notes: If it were redeemed, the money would buy a new animal. That new animal is not the wicked person's own offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ: כִּי אָמְרִינַן זֶבַח רְשָׁעִים תּוֹעֵבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק applies only to the original animal. A redeemed and replaced offering has changed, so the פסוק does not apply to it.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: 'its animals' excludes בכור and מעשר
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with רבי שמעון, who learns from the word 'its animals' that בכור and מעשר animals are not destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'Its animals' means its own animals, and not firstborn or tithe animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the next part of the ברייתא, which is a new teaching of רבי שמעון. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק commands destroying the city's animals. רבי שמעון reads 'its animals' narrowly, so בכור and מעשר are left out. The גמרא will now ask what kind of בכור and מעשר he means.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Its animals' (the city's animals, from the פסוק about עיר הנדחת)
A firstborn kosher animal, holy and given to a כהן
Animal tithe, every tenth animal, which is holy

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
'Its animals' and not firstborn or tithe animals.
phrases.notes: The word comes from the פסוק about the condemned city, דברים 13:16.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: בְּהֶמְתָּהּ וְלֹא בֶּהֱמַת בְּכוֹר וּמַעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בכור and מעשר animals of an עיר הנדחת are not destroyed, learned from the word 'בהמתה.'

steps.title: Unblemished or blemished? Neither seems to fit
steps.stepSummary: If רבי שמעון means unblemished animals, they belong to Heaven and need no פסוק. If he means blemished ones, they belong to the owners and should be destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we talking about? If unblemished animals, they are Heaven's spoils anyway. If blemished animals, they are the city's spoils, so why exclude them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of בכור and מעשר רבי שמעון means. Each possible answer seems to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unblemished בכור and מעשר are offerings and belong to Heaven, so they were never the city's property and need no exclusion. Blemished ones may be eaten by their owners like ordinary property. So they should be destroyed with the rest of the city's spoils, and רבי שמעון's exclusion seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with?
If you say
Unblemished animals, fit for the altar
Spoils of Heaven, which are not destroyed
Blemished animals

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If we say with unblemished animals,
they are the spoils of Heaven!
Rather, with blemished animals,
are they not its spoils?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the case of רבי שמעון's teaching from Step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's exclusion of בכור and מעשר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A double bind: unblemished animals need no exclusion, and blemished animals are private property that should be destroyed.

steps.title: רבינא: blemished בכור and מעשר are eaten as holy, not as the city's
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון means blemished animals. Even blemished, בכור and מעשר are eaten under their holy status, so they count as Heaven's spoils.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: Really it is about blemished animals. 'Its animals' means animals eaten as the city's own animals. That excludes these, which are eaten as בכור and מעשר, because they are Heaven's spoils.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the challenge. He picks the blemished case and explains why those animals still are not counted as the city's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished בכור or מעשר may be eaten, but only under its holy status as a בכור or מעשר, never as an ordinary animal. Since its identity stays holy, it counts as Heaven's spoils and not 'its animals.' So the word 'בהמתה' rightly excludes it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (keeping one of the options)
Under the status or category of
Excluded are

steps.whatToRemember: Blemished בכור and מעשר are eaten as holy animals, not as plain property. So they are שלל שמים and are not destroyed with the עיר הנדחת.
steps.confusionAlert: A blemish does not make a בכור or מעשר ordinary. It may be eaten, but it keeps its holy status, which is why רבינא counts it as Heaven's spoils.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
Actually, with blemished animals,
and it means what is eaten under the status of 'its animals.'
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק only destroys animals that are eaten as the city people's own ordinary animals.

phrases.english: Excluded are these
which are not eaten under the status of 'its animals,'
but rather under the status of firstborn and tithe,
for they are the spoils of Heaven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the double-bind קשיא of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the double bind and refines what 'בהמתה' means
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Blemished בכור and מעשר are ordinary property of the city and should be destroyed.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are eaten only under their holy status, so they are שלל שמים and are excluded by 'בהמתה.'

steps.title: This disagrees with שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that what was just said disagrees with שמואל, who said: everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this disagrees with שמואל, because שמואל said: Everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the explanation just given does not match a statement of שמואל. It quotes שמואל's short statement, which sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's words are very short and unclear: 'everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed.' The גמרא brings them up because they seem to point to a different approach from the one just given for בכור and מעשר. Before going further, the גמרא needs to explain what שמואל means.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees (with)
Is sacrificed on the מזבח
Is redeemed (its holiness is moved onto money)

phrases.english: And this disagrees with שמואל,
phrases.notes: 'This' refers to the answer about blemished בכור and מעשר in the step just before.

phrases.english: for שמואל said:
Everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the answer of step 15 with a statement of שמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed.

steps.title: What does שמואל mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שמואל's short statement means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for an explanation of שמואל's unclear words. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read literally, 'everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed' cannot be true, because some holy animals, like a בכור, are never redeemed. So the גמרא asks what שמואל really means.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying?

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the statement quoted in step 16
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of שמואל's statement 'everything is sacrificed and everything is redeemed'

steps.title: Two groups of holy animals, two sources
steps.stepSummary: שמואל means this: animals that are sacrificed when unblemished and redeemed when blemished are excluded by the word 'its spoils.' Animals that are sacrificed but not redeemed, like בכור and מעשר, are excluded by the word 'its animals.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he means: Any animal that is sacrificed when it is unblemished, and redeemed when it has a blemish, is excluded by the word 'its spoils.' And any animal that is sacrificed when it is unblemished but is not redeemed when it has a blemish, such as a בכור or מעשר, is learned from the word 'its animals.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains שמואל's words. He is sorting holy animals into two groups, and each group is excluded from destruction by a different word in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Group one: ordinary קדשים, which are sacrificed when whole and redeemed when blemished. These are excluded by the word 'שללה' because they belong to Heaven. Group two: בכור and מעשר, which are never redeemed even with a blemish. Their exclusion comes from 'בהמתה.' שמואל applies this even to unblemished בכור and מעשר, while רבינא (step 15) needed the blemished case, and that is the disagreement noted in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: Unblemished (fit for the מזבח)
An animal with a blemish
'Its spoils' (word in the פסוק about עיר הנדחת)
'Its animals' (word in the פסוק about עיר הנדחת)
A firstborn animal and an animal tithe

steps.whatToRemember: There are two kinds of holy animals in an עיר הנדחת. Those that can be redeemed are excluded by 'שללה'. בכור and מעשר, which cannot be redeemed, are excluded by 'בהמתה'.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
Any animal that is sacrificed when it is unblemished,
and is redeemed when it has a blemish,
is excluded by 'its spoils,'
and any animal that is sacrificed when it is unblemished
and is not redeemed when it has a blemish,
such as a firstborn or an animal tithe,
is learned from 'its animals.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Redeemable קדשים are excluded by 'שללה'; בכור and מעשר, which are not redeemable, are excluded by 'בהמתה'.

steps.title: רב חסדא: which תרומה is left to rot
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says תרומות in an עיר הנדחת must be left to rot. רב חסדא says this applies only to תרומה still held by a ישראל. תרומה already held by a כהן is his property, so it must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'תרומות must be left to rot.' רב חסדא said: They taught this only about תרומה in the hands of a ישראל. But תרומה in the hands of a כהן is his own property, so it must be burned.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the ברייתא, about תרומה found in the condemned city. רב חסדא limits that rule to one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything that belongs to the people of the city is burned. A ישראל does not really own תרומה, since it must go to a כהן, so it is not burned and is just left to rot. A כהן does own his תרומה, so it counts as the city's property and is burned.

keyTerms.meaning: The portion of produce given to a כהן
Must be left to rot
They taught this only (about a certain case)
Must be burned

phrases.english: 'תרומות must be left to rot.'
רב חסדא said:
They taught this only
about תרומה in the hands of a ישראל,
but תרומה in the hands of a כהן,
since it is his property,
must be burned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new clause of the ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תרומה held by a ישראל is left to rot; תרומה held by a כהן is his property and is burned.

steps.title: רב יוסף: מעשר שני is hidden away, not burned
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף objects. The משנה says מעשר שני is hidden away. Yet מעשר שני held by a ישראל is like תרומה held by a כהן, so according to רב חסדא it should be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: 'מעשר שני and holy writings must be hidden away.' But מעשר שני in the hands of a ישראל is just like תרומה in the hands of a כהן, and still the משנה teaches that it is hidden away!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף challenges רב חסדא using the משנה's rule about מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל may eat his מעשר שני, so it is a lot like a כהן with his תרומה. If owning it makes it 'city property' that gets burned, then מעשר שני should be burned too. But the משנה says it is hidden away. That suggests owning holy food does not make it get burned, which goes against רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, eaten by its owner in ירושלים
Must be hidden away (stored, not destroyed by burning)
Holy writings (scrolls of תנ"ך)

phrases.english: רב יוסף raised an objection:
'מעשר שני and holy writings must be hidden away.'
But מעשר שני in the hands of a ישראל
is like תרומה in the hands of a כהן,
and it teaches that they must be hidden away!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's statement in step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that a כהן's תרומה is burned because it is his property
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מעשר שני owned by a ישראל is the same kind of case, yet the משנה says it is hidden away and not burned.

steps.title: רב חסדא's statement, reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רב חסדא's statement. 'Left to rot' refers to תרומה held by a כהן. תרומה still held by a ישראל should be given to a כהן in another city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said: רב חסדא said: They taught this only about תרומה in the hands of a כהן. But תרומה in the hands of a ישראל should be given to a כהן in another city.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the objection stands, the גמרא says רב חסדא's statement must have been worded differently. It gives the corrected version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the כהן's תרומה is treated like מעשר שני: it keeps its holiness, so it is not burned and is just left to rot. A ישראל's תרומה was never really his, so it is not destroyed at all. Instead, it is given to a כהן who lives elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a corrected version of a statement)
Another city

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the corrected version, 'left to rot' is about the כהן's תרומה, and the ישראל's תרומה is given away. No תרומה is burned anymore.
steps.whatToRemember: In the final version of רב חסדא's statement, a כהן's תרומה is left to rot, and a ישראל's תרומה is given to a כהן in another city.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא, לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
phrases.english: רב חסדא said: They taught this only
about תרומה in the hands of a כהן,
but תרומה in the hands of a ישראל
should be given to a כהן in another city.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection by changing the wording of רב חסדא's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Restating the statement in a different version
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A כהן's תרומה is his property, so it is burned with the city's goods.
steps.terutzMaskana: A כהן's תרומה keeps its holiness like מעשר שני and is left to rot; a ישראל's תרומה is given to a כהן elsewhere.

steps.title: Is מעשר שני dough obligated in חלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a teaching from elsewhere: רבי מאיר says מעשר שני dough is exempt from חלה, and the חכמים say it is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned there: Dough made of מעשר שני is exempt from חלה. These are the words of רבי מאיר. And the חכמים say it is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related dispute about מעשר שני. This sets up רב חסדא's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps asked whether a ישראל really owns his מעשר שני. This dispute about חלה touches the same question, which is why the גמרא brings it here.

keyTerms.meaning: Dough
The portion of dough given to a כהן
Rule that it is obligated

phrases.english: We learned there:
Dough made of מעשר שני
is exempt from challah,
these are the words of רבי מאיר.
And the חכמים say it is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a related dispute about the status of מעשר שני
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: מעשר שני dough is exempt from challah; חכמים: it is obligated.

steps.title: רב חסדא: the dispute is only in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא says the dispute is about מעשר שני in ירושלים. רבי מאיר holds it is ממון גבוה, and the רבנן hold it is ממון הדיוט. Outside ירושלים, everyone agrees it is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: The dispute is about מעשר שני in ירושלים. רבי מאיר holds that מעשר שני is property of the Most High, and the רבנן hold that it is ordinary property. But in the outlying areas, everyone agrees it is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains where the dispute applies and what it depends on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים the owner may eat מעשר שני. So the question is whether it still belongs to Heaven (exempt) or counts as the owner's own property (obligated in challah). Outside ירושלים he may not eat it at all, so it is clearly not his. That is why everyone agrees it is exempt there.

keyTerms.meaning: Property belonging to Heaven
Ordinary, non-holy property of a person
Areas outside ירושלים
Everyone agrees

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר holds מעשר שני is ממון גבוה, and the רבנן hold it is ממון הדיוט. This argument only applies in ירושלים; outside ירושלים, all agree the dough is exempt from חלה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The question of whether מעשר שני is ממון גבוה or ממון הדיוט comes up in many areas of הלכה, including the earlier question of how to treat it in an עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: רב חסדא said:
The dispute is about מעשר שני in ירושלים,
for רבי מאיר holds
that מעשר שני is property of the Most High,
and the רבנן hold that it is ordinary property.
But in the outlying areas,
everyone agrees it is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מַחְלוֹקֶת בְּמַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the dispute in step 22 applies and what it depends on
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only in ירושלים and depends on ממון גבוה vs. ממון הדיוט; outside ירושלים, all agree it is exempt.

steps.title: רב יוסף quotes the משנה about hiding מעשר שני
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף opens a challenge to רב חסדא by quoting the משנה: in an עיר הנדחת, מעשר שני and holy scrolls are hidden away.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף raises an objection: מעשר שני and holy writings must be hidden away.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף quotes the משנה to start an objection against רב חסדא. The full challenge is built step by step in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא said that outside ירושלים, מעשר שני belongs to Heaven (ממון גבוה). Things that belong to Heaven are not counted as the city's property. Yet the משנה treats מעשר שני as forbidden and hides it away, as if it belonged to the people of the city.

keyTerms.meaning: holy writings, meaning scrolls of תנ"ך
they must be hidden away (put in גניזה)

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raises an objection:
Second tithe and holy writings must be hidden away.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's claim in step 23 that outside ירושלים מעשר שני is ממון גבוה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's claim that outside ירושלים מעשר שני is ממון גבוה according to everyone
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Hiding it away shows it is forbidden as the city's property, which fits ממון הדיוט, not ממון גבוה.

steps.title: Could the משנה be talking about ירושלים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the משנה means. It suggests ירושלים, but asks how ירושלים could ever become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with? If you say it is in ירושלים, can ירושלים become an עיר הנדחת?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants to pin down the case in the משנה. It tests the first option, ירושלים, and doubts it right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה were about ירושלים, רב חסדא would have no problem, because in ירושלים there is a dispute about whether מעשר שני is the owner's property. So the גמרא checks whether ירושלים is even possible as a setting.

keyTerms.meaning: what case are we dealing with?
if you say
a city whose people turned to עבודה זרה and is destroyed

phrases.english: What are we dealing with?
If you say in Jerusalem,
can it become an idolatrous city?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins narrowing down the case of the משנה that רב יוסף quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what location is the משנה's מעשר שני found?

steps.title: A ברייתא shows ירושלים can never become an עיר הנדחת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא lists ten special rules for ירושלים. One of them is that ירושלים can never become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.simpleTranslation: But a ברייתא teaches: ten things were said about ירושלים, and this is one of them: it does not become an עיר הנדחת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the ירושלים option is impossible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים can never be an עיר הנדחת, so the משנה cannot be about מעשר שני inside ירושלים. This removes the easy way out for רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: ten special rules

phrases.english: But it was taught: Ten things were said about Jerusalem,
and this is one of them –
it does not become an idolatrous city!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs the doubt raised in step 25, ruling out ירושלים.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה cannot be about מעשר שני inside ירושלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing ten special laws of ירושלים

steps.title: Produce taken up to ירושלים is no longer tied to the city
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests produce from another city that was brought into ירושלים. It rejects this, because once ירושלים's walls take in the produce, it no longer belongs to the doomed city.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is from another city, and they brought it up into ירושלים? But the walls already took it in!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second setting and rejects it too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the produce entered ירושלים's walls, it was taken in by ירושלים and is separate from the עיר הנדחת. In that case there would be no reason to hide it.

keyTerms.meaning: they brought it up inside (ירושלים)
the walls took it in

phrases.english: Rather, in a different city,
and they brought it up into it?
phrases.notes: "Into it" means into ירושלים, before the other city became an עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: But the walls took it in!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ירושלים is ruled out, a second setting is tested and rejected.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the משנה is about produce brought up to ירושלים
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The walls of ירושלים already took the produce in, so it is no longer connected to the doomed city.

steps.title: So the משנה must be about produce outside ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: With both options gone, the משנה must be about מעשר שני outside ירושלים. Yet it is hidden away, which goes against רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it about produce outside ירושלים, and it teaches that it must be hidden away?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב יוסף's challenge. The only setting left is produce outside ירושלים, and that is exactly where רב חסדא said it is Heaven's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside ירושלים, רב חסדא said that everyone agrees מעשר שני is ממון גבוה. But the משנה forbids it and hides it away like the city's own property, which fits ממון הדיוט. So the משנה seems to contradict רב חסדא.

keyTerms.meaning: rather, isn't it...
areas outside ירושלים

phrases.english: Rather, is it not in the outlying areas,
and it teaches: they must be hidden away?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge's conclusion after the other settings were eliminated.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Outside ירושלים, hiding the produce away shows it is the owner's property, against רב חסדא's claim that it is ממון גבוה.

steps.title: The case is produce in ירושלים that became impure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is about produce from another city that was brought up to ירושלים. It is hidden away only because it became impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it really is from another city and they brought it up into ירושלים. And what case is this? Where it became impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב חסדא. It goes back to the setting it rejected earlier and adds one detail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The produce is hidden away because impure מעשר שני cannot be eaten, not because it belongs to the עיר הנדחת. So the משנה proves nothing about whose property it is.

keyTerms.meaning: really, actually (going back to an earlier option)
that became ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: In step 27 the גמרא rejected the ירושלים case. Here it goes back to that same case. That works because the reason for hiding the produce has changed: it is now impurity, not the עיר הנדחת.

phrases.english: No, actually it is from a different city,
and they brought it up into it.
And what are we dealing with here? Where it became impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge by bringing back the ירושלים case from step 27 with an added detail.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hiding away showed that מעשר שני outside ירושלים is the owner's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: The hiding away is because of impurity in ירושלים, so רב חסדא stands.

steps.title: Why not redeem the impure מעשר שני?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the impure produce is not simply redeemed. רבי אלעזר taught that impure מעשר שני can be redeemed even inside ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him redeem it! For רבי אלעזר said: from where do we know that מעשר שני that became impure may be redeemed even in ירושלים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the produce is impure, it should be redeemed, not hidden away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says impure מעשר שני may be redeemed even inside ירושלים. If so, impurity is no reason to hide it, and the answer in step 29 seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: let him redeem it
we redeem (move the holiness onto money)
from where do we know?

phrases.english: And let him redeem it?
For Rabbi Elazar said:
From where do we know regarding second tithe that became impure
that we redeem it even in Jerusalem?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the impurity answer of step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the produce is hidden because it became impure
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Impure מעשר שני can be redeemed even in ירושלים, so it should not need to be hidden away.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: "שאת" means eating
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns his rule from the פסוק "לא תוכל שאתו". He reads שאת as eating, based on a פסוק about portions of food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "you cannot carry it," and "שאת" means eating, as it says "and he took portions from before him."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting רבי אלעזר's proof, which backs up the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק allows redeeming מעשר שני when "you cannot שאת it." Since שאת means eating, any מעשר שני that cannot be eaten, including impure produce, may be redeemed. This applies even inside ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches
carrying; here read as eating
portions of food

phrases.english: The verse states: "You will not be able to carry it,"
and "se'et" means nothing other than eating,
as it is said: "And he took portions from before him."
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:34. Those portions were food, so the same root points to eating.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי אלעזר's rule that powers the challenge in step 30.
steps.raayaObject: That impure מעשר שני may be redeemed even in ירושלים
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברים 14:24, with שאת explained from בראשית 43:34

steps.title: The case is food bought with מעשר שני money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is about food bought with מעשר שני money that became impure. That kind of food is hidden away rather than redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Something bought with מעשר שני money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case even more. רב חסדא's view is saved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule covers the original מעשר שני produce. Here the case is food that was bought with מעשר שני money and then became impure, which is not redeemed but hidden away. So hiding it away is still about impurity, not about the עיר הנדחת.

keyTerms.meaning: something bought with מעשר שני money

steps.whatToRemember: רב יוסף tried to prove from the משנה that מעשר שני outside ירושלים is private property. The גמרא answered that the משנה is about food bought with מעשר שני money, brought into ירושלים, that became impure. It is hidden away because it cannot be eaten, so רב חסדא's view stands.

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here? With something purchased.
phrases.notes: He means food bought with מעשר שני money, not the original produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redemption challenge of steps 30–31 by narrowing the case of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Impure מעשר שני should be redeemed, so the impurity answer fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case is impure food bought with מעשר שני money, which is not redeemed, so it is hidden away.
